newsitem.title: USA: IMF SAYS KENYA MUST TACKLE CORRUPTION FOR IMF CASH.
newsitem.headline: IMF SAYS KENYA MUST TACKLE CORRUPTION FOR IMF CASH.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund, responding to comments that Kenya might look for talks on a new loan, said on Thursday that Nairobi had to deal with "governance issues" before new lending talks could start.

The IMF halted its Kenya loan program last week due to concern about corruption. A spokesman said on Thursday that the IMF was happy to offer Kenya technical advice, but was worried by issues behind its decision to halt the earlier loan, the first year of an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility.
"The fund is ready to assist Kenya with policy advice, including developing a framework to deal with the current situation," the spokesman said.

But he added: "Any formal fund involvement in support of Kenya's economic reform program will hinge upon fundamental measures to address governance issues raised earlier in the context of the first year ESAF review."
The IMF's decision to halt its lending program sent Kenyan financial markets into a tailspin and the shilling plunged to a new official low of 70.26 to the dollar on Thursday.

In Nairobi, Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi said that Kenya was considering talks with the IMF on securing a second year of the loan arrangement, which he said was "still available." He said the government was committed to sound fiscal and monetary policies.
